topics.title: Short lived account detected
topics.content:
Description: The alert triggers when any username created and deleted within a short period of time, technically which is 5 minutes. Which will be detected using event ID 4720 followed by event ID 4726

 

Log source: Windows event logs, Active directory logs.

 

Gathering information: date and time, source user and user, source IP, host name.

 

Analysis:  we will start with validating the source user detail who performed the creation and deletion of the account by correlating the source IP and source user by using username look up dashboard and hostname look up dashboard.

 

  • If we observe the source user belongs to the active directory(AD) or IAM team, where both have authorization for creating the account. 
  • I will do further analysis with validation by co-relating with other log source like checking the supportive ticket for deleted account or checking the outlook for any prior notifications. Then we will reach out to the user over Microsoft teams to get the business justification of the activity.
  • Based on the source user response we mention the analysis detail in a closure comment and we close the alert as false positive.
  • Technically our client has this use case as a part of validation alert.
  • As part auditing of the alert i observe one of the alerts which is closed as false positive where the source user belongs to the active directory team but the user does not have authorization to create the account but the alert is closed as false positive by mentioning the closure comment which says that user belongs to active directory.
  • Here the analyst did not carry out the further analysis step like, reaching out to the user or creating the supportive ticket.
  • Then I reopen the ticket added to the active directory admin and our manager in the same ticket to inform about the misconfiguration with the authorization to create the account.
  • A further active directory team changed the configuration to reduce the authorized account creation activity.
  • I prepared the report on this incident and presented it during the weekly team meeting for which I got appreciation from our manager.

topics.title: New user added to admin group.
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when any user created which can be identified with the help of event ID 4720 and if the same user added to admin group which can be identified with event ID 4732

 

Log source: active directory logs, windows event logs.

 

Gathering information: source user details, account details, source IP and host name.

 

Analysis:  The alert is configured based on the Mittre Attack persistence, which means the attacker might have created the account and added to the privilege or admin group to have greater access so that the attacker can perform CRUD.

 

  •  We will check the source IP used in the activity to make sure whether it is performed by using public IP or Private IP.
  • We need to verify the host involved in the activity whether the host involved in the activity is a managed or unmanaged device. then we will verify the source user who performed the creation and adding of the user to the admin group. Whether the function of the source user is authorised to perform the activity.
  • We will look for any supportive ticket or emails for the user for which account has been created and added to the admin group.
  • Once we will verify all attributes we will take further actions.

Example:

  1. If the internal IP is detected as a source and managed device involved in the activity, the source user is authorized to perform the activity.
  2. If we have a supportive ticket related to a new employee joining the organisation we can close the alert as benign by mentioning the reference ticket number and adding the detailed closure comment carried during the analysis.

topics.title: user reported phishing email.
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when more than 3 users reported any email as phishing mail within six hours.

 

 Log source: ESA => Microsoft 365 defender

 

Gathering Info: sender domain, sender mail, address, source IP, subject and receiver details.

 

Analysis:  once the alert triggers o n the incident review dashboard when reported by more than 3 users, we will start validating the reputation of sender domain and associated IP address. By using offline analysis method which include checking the reputation OS INT too;s like virus total, abuse IPDB, IPVoid, MXTools box

  • In our organization we use MS 365 defender as ESA through which we will perform complete email analysis.
  • Once we log in to defender, under email and collaboration in explorer we can filter out the reported mail by using subject line, sender mail address and sender domain.
  • Once we filter out the detected email, we open the email in a new tab to perform complete analysis.
  • In analysis we will validate the sender and recipient details followed by checking the return path and return path domain to validate whether the email is spoofed or not
  • Then we will validate the email authenticate, SPF, DKIM and DMARC.

SPF:  sender policy framework which helps to authenticate whether the mail came from an authenticated user or not by comparing the domain name to IP address.

DKIM: domain key identifying mail which helps to validate the integrity of the mail to make sure the mail is not tampered while following through the different mail server by checking the cryptographic signatures.

DMARC: Domain based message authentication reporting conformance which is the combination of SPF and DKIM.

  • In the meantime we will perform header analysis using Microsoft message header analysis. Apart from this we will also validate related entities like attachment and URLs.
  • Once we click the detected attachment, the defender will give the analysis details and we can also perform the offline analysis by capturing the hash value of the detected file. In the same way we will change the URL in the detected email.

Action and recommendation:

  1. If any negative attributes are observed with respect to the analysis like negative email authentication, negative domain and IP reputation, negative attachment and URL detected we create the incident to purge the email from all the users in_boxes to the ESA team.
  2. We also recommend a proxy and firewall team to block the domain and IP respectively.

Scenario:  if any user found to clicked on any URL that can be identified in URL clicks

 

Then we will check the user activity with respect to login activity to make sure user credentials has not been shared and also we will write the email to user to reset the password

 

If any attachment has been downloaded by the user, we will recommend the EDR team or will create a scan to check the disposition of the file.

 

If any user clicked the url(phishing URL)

If it is malicious to ensure there are any other users clicked on the same URL by going into advanced hunting in defender there we will write the query by referring the URL click events and run it for detected URL. which will give number of users who clicked on the URL so that we can add all the other users to reset the credentials and revolve all active sessions and create the scan on the host to ensure no malicious files were downloaded.

topics.title: Potential malicious URL clicked detection
topics.content:
Description: The alert triggers when any user clicks on the URL which is flagged as malicious by O365(Office 365)

 

Log source: Microsoft 365 defender.

 

Gathering Info: host name, user details, source IP, URl details and action.

 

Analysis: 

  1. The analysis starts from checking the URL details while logging into the defender where we can find the email which delivered the malicious URL.
  2. Then we will perform the basic header analysis which includes checking sender and recipient details, delivery action, original location, latest delivery location, associated IP address and email authenticates value like, SPF, DKM and DMARC.
  3. Then we will check the reputation of the URL using the OSINT tools like Virus total.
  4. Then by using the sandbox environment KASM tool we will try to check what the URL belongs to.
  5. Before that we will download the original email using O365 to  understand what the email content looks like.
  6. While working on one of the alerts we absorb that URL directing to download a PDF file where the same PDF file is sent as an attachment in the email also.
  7. To verify the attachment. We downloaded the file from the KASM environment and submitted the file into the TRELLICS sandbox to get the detailed file analysis report.
  8. In this particular alert the URL is clean but the PDF file also contains an URL which is taking the user to a phishing site hence we confirm the detection as true positive.
  9. As a part of recommendation we need to verify if any other users are delivered the same email.
  10. By using advanced hunting as a defender. We observe three other users who get delivered with the same email and only that detected user clicked on the URL.
  11. As a precautionary measures we created the ticket to reset the user credential and revoke the running session 
  12. Then we created another ticket to the network team to block the IP in the firewall, URL in proxy and ESA team to purge the email from all the user inboxes.

topics.title: An IP address matched a crowdstrike intelligence indicator that has previously been used in targeted attack.
topics.content:
Description : the alert triggers when internal host communications with the malicious IP address which is stored in the database of the Falcon.

 

Log source: EDR.

 

 Gather information:  hostname, src IP, user details, user agent.

 

 Analysis:  

  1. analysis starts from checking the reputation of detected IP by using OSINT tools like virustotal, IPvoid and AbuseIPDB
  2. Then by going into endpoint detection in falcon, we try to understand the triggering condition.
  3. Then we will look into the command line associated with the detection which helps to identify the user agent associated with the detection.
  4. Then we need to go into host investigation to identify the root cause of the connections
  5. We will export the DNS request in the last CSV format for last 24 hours to match the timeline of the connection.
  6. Once we match with the timeline of DNS request, we observe that the user was accessing some construction website, which redirected to a malicious domain which is assigned detection.
  7. To verify that we open the URL in @KASM which can not be accessed at the time, then we try to access the construction website and do the inspection on the browser which confirmed that from the construction URL user redirected to detection drafts observing the alert.
  8. To ensure any downloads or connections we further try to connect to the host in EDR
  9. To check the download folder we run the command cd/users/hostname/downloads
  10. Then by using ls(list) command we can get the list of downloads in the host.
  11. Since the detected URL can not be accessed no downloads drops are observed.
  12. As a part of remediation, since malicious URL has been accessed we created the ticket to reset the browser and also created one more ticket for blocking URL in proxy and IP in firewall
  13. At the end we also send security communication to user about secure device usage policy.

Updated on 24-12-2025

  1. In crowdstrike EDR to identify where the file got downloaded we can use the event search in investigation there we can search using the file name which will give the events related to the file.
  2. From the events we can search for the event's simple name which is motwWitten which will give the details about the route of the file from where it entered the system which contains the information like host URL and referral URL.

topics.title: O365(office 365) MFA phone removed.
topics.content:
Description:  This rule O365 MFA phone removed is triggered when a change in MFA configuration is detected.

 

Log source: O365 logs, active directory.

 

Gathering information:  Target username, target user email ID, Timestamp, result of action.

 

Analysis:  By using the targeted user email address, I log into Microsoft Azure Entra ID which we use as our active directory, I will check in the overview and in properties section to verify any mobile number is listed in the user details.

  1. I will goto auditlog of the user in the relevant time frame. ill look for the activity type “admin detected security info”. Here I will investigate the details like timestamp, status reason (admin deleted phone method for user) initiated actor and IP address.
  2. I'll analyse the reputation of the IP address using OSINT tools.
  3. I will check the details of the initiated actor in Azure Entra ID whether he is a privileged account holder or not and send him a mail to verify the activity and request for the business justification and also confirm if any supportive ticket is involved in the change.
  4. If the initiator confirms the activity that they updated the phone number or device of MFA authentication and obtained the manager approval, and requests the admin to update the new number for authentication then we close this alert as benign.
  5. If the actor is unresponsive or if the IP is malicious then will escalate this to the IT team to disable the account to prevent further unauthorised access.
  6. Investigate users account activity for any suspicious action that may have occurred during the period when MFA was disabled.
  7. If the user’s email address was changed, reset the email address to the original value and also investigate the reason for the change and ensure it was authorised.

topics.title: attempt to download a malicious file from CLI (command Line Interface)
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when any host tries to download the files using the CIRL command.

 

Log source: EDR ->crowdstrike falcon.

 

Gathering information: host name, user details, domain, URL or IP address.

 

 

Analysis: as part of analysis we logged into crowdstrike falcon thereby using the hostname we will filter out the detection.

  1. Once we go into full detection details. We can get the complete details about the alert.
  2. The detection IOA is tagged as CURLGETMalware download.
  3. Then we look into command line associated with the trigger where we identify as github-related URL accessed from the user host
  4. The URL from github trying to download a file where the naming is identified as minor which ensures that the user tried to download the coin miner file from github.
  5. As we went into the process table we identified that the command executed by the node process which runs the CURL command.
  6. As the URL pointing towards the crypto miner setup file the technique involves an attempt to download & execution of the malicious file.
  7. The crowdstrike has killed the process to prevent the script from execution.
  8. As the action clearly attempted to crypto miner on the server indicates possible compromise of the application service or user account running on the server.
  9. As a precautionary measure we network contained the host from the EDR and created a scan on the host.
  10. We escalated the case to the client then involved in a bridge call with our client, the principal analyst POC from the client and SOC team.
  11. In the bridge call analysis we identified that the suspected server contains a vulnerability which is pre-authentication remote code execution as the component version is older.
  12. Since the vulnerability related to pre-authenticated RCE(Remote code execution) we observed http requests from the server. Hence, the user account involved in the activity is also requested to disable.

topics.title: public hosted zone created
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when any route 53 zone was created and selected as a public.

 

Log source: AWS

 

Mittre tactic: initial access

 

Gathering info: user details, src IP, Host name and domain name.

 

 

Analysis: as the alert related to the cloud environment the alert will be triggered based on the signals. Which in this case is the creation of a public zone.

 

  1.  I will try to validate the access chain related to the activity where we need to verify the user details, user details, time, the activity, IP address related to the activity, geolocation and user agent.
  2. Once we verify the role of the user, we will verify the events or activity related to create, update, delete, read.
  3. Continuing to that we will verify the success, failed and unauthorized events related to CRUD.
  4. Then we will reach out to the user to get to know about the awareness and business justification for the activity.
  5. As per the role suggestion we need confirmation from the user as the hosted zone is in public which may be caused due to the misconfiguration which may lead to unauthorized exploitation.

topics.title: Azure AD suspicious sign-on
topics.content:
Description:  the alert triggers when an user signin to an account in unusual or risky way.

 

 

Log source: Active directory microsoft azure Entra ID.

 

Gathering information:  user account, location, host involved, time of sign in, sign in location, device used, application accessed, sign in status(failed or successful).

 

 

Analysis:  ill login to the active directory using the user account, i will check on the overview and in the property section will investigate the details of the user like, his designation, department, when was the password changed absorbed, base location and his manager.

 

  1. Now I'll start analysing sing-in logs of the user by matching the time provided in the alert. I'll check the reputation of the IP address by using an offline analysis method and also try to find if it belongs to any VPN.
  2. I'll compare the login location with the user's usual work location to see if it matches.
  3. I'll investigate the device used by the user(mobile or laptop) and browser used during the login and check if it is a registered device (managed device) or not.
  4. Ill check the sign in status to see if was successful or interested or failure and note the reason if the was failure
  5. Ill check if MFA was completed and if any conditional access policies were applied
  6. If we find anything unusual for the user like new IP, location, or unregistered device or MFA was not completed, ill email to user’s manager to confirm the activity and also suggest them to use the different mode of communication other than mail, will create a ticket with all the information during by investigation and attaching proof of evidence collected.
  7. If I receive confirmation from the manager that the user performing the activity will close the alert as false positive.
  8. If we can't validate the sign-in activity with in 24 hours or if the user denies the activity, ill treat the login as suspicious, we will revoke all the active sessions, reset the user's password and send the mail to IT team to assist the user in account recovery and also notify the users manager. Now I will close the alert as a true positive.
  9. If i observe any negative attributes such as malicious IP address, usage of VPN from country of concern, multiple MFA failures, multiple failed login attempt, sign in from multiple countries with in short period of time, ill treat it as malicious activity and immediately I will revoke all the session and reset the user’s password and inform the helpdesk team to assist the user account recovery.

topics.title: Access from unusual user agent(browser)
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when any user tries to access an internal resource by using undefined user agent(browser).

 

Log source:  Proxy

 

Gathering info: source IP, host detail, user detail, destination url, http response code, HTTP method, action, bytes sent and bytes received, user agent details.

 

Analysis: since the alert triggered for an unusual user agent, we start with validating the IP involved in the activity to verify if it is private IP or Private IP.

  1. We need to check the user agent involved in the activity whether it is permitted or not. Eg: in our client environment the unmanaged devices are allowed to connect to authorization by using secured browser called
  2. Then we will check when the user joined the organization by using the username look-up dashboard.
  3. If the user found to be joined recently. We will raise the request by creating a ticket to the manager of the detected user to request access for the dedicated browser to communicate with the organisation.
  4. On other case if external IP detected in the alert first we need to validate the IP reputation and geolocation details by using OSINT tools like virus total, abuse IPDB and IP void
  5. If the detected IP found to be malicious or location belongs to out of the business core of our client we recommend to block the IP in all segments of the firewall.
  6. Sometimes we detect the VPN segment IP but users are using the unauthorised user agent. We write the event to the user by providing all the default user agents to the talon browser by providing steps to change the process.

topics.title: Multiple requests to DGA (Domain generative algorithm) domain indicating infection.
topics.content:
DGA: it's a program used by malware to generate a large number of domain name requests with C2C (command and control).

 

Description : the alert triggers when the internal system tries to connect with multiple domains which may look like related to IP loop-up service(DNS Server).

 

Log source:  Proxy and NBA (network behaviour analysis) tool alpha SOC

 

Gathering info:  Source IP, hostname, user details, URL, Action.

 

Analysis: the analysis starts from gathering info about user designation and department to ensure it does not belong to the information security department so that we can rule out the alert as benign.

 

  1. Next we need to check the base file, filename. Which created the domain request, to verify that either we can go with searching the log siem, splunk search or by going into the host repository in crowdstrike falcon (EDR).
  2. In crowdstrike falcon we’ll go into host management by using host name we’ll download networking activity related to domain request in CSV format, there we’ll perform defiltering to validate further.
  3. In this particular alert the request created by chrome browser, user trying to access some gaming website but that landed into a different page.
  4. Next we need to check the domain reputation by using OSINT tools and found around 3 engines reported this domain as malicious.
  5. To verify the authenticity of the URL we try to access the URL in KASM where we got the result as 404 not found. We did the same activity for other detected domains which resulted the same.
  6. As per the analysis it is detected that user tries to access some gaming website which landed into untrusted domains and alert got triggered when we check the action taken by the proxy found to be benign
  7. Once we have the root cause as a part of precautionary measure we created the ticket to enterprise security admin team to reset the chrome browser and also created one more ticket to block the malicious domain detected in the alert and also informed the user about the device usage policy like not to connect to untrusted domain using managed devices, we close this alert as true positive

topics.title: multiple file transfer to external domain.
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when any internal user transfers the file to external domain which is detected by MS PURVIEW DLP POLICY

 

Log source: MSPURVIEWDLP(Data loss prevention).

 

Gathering information: user details, destination domain details, file details.

 

Analysis: since it is a DLP alert we work on these alerts when escalated by the external DLP support team.

 

  1.  Once we get the escalation we will start looking into notes provided in the escalation. In one of the alerts we observed that the user was uploading the file to an AI website.
  2. Then we start looking into detected files by the DLP policy which will be provided by the DLP support team in the form of CSV.
  3. We will go and verify the files to identify by the file name to make a decision on the security of the content.
  4. Sometimes it is difficult to make decisions based on the filename then we will drop the security notification to the user's manager to validate the file sensitivity.
  5. While having the conversation with the user we get to know that the user didn't upload the files to the AI domain, but the user is using one of the AI extensions which uploaded the files to another domain.
  6. With this observation we created the ticket and also looped our internal trusted AI team to define the policies related to using AI within the organisation environment.

topics.title: process triggered for a high severity custom rule.
topics.content:
Description:  we have some custom IOA rules configured in crowdstrike EDR for some domains, files and IP addresses. Whenever any alert matches the custom IOA detection, the alert will trigger.

 

Log source: EDR => crowdstrike falcon.

 

Gathering information: user details, host details.

 

Analysis: whenever the custom IOA detection happens, we will go into crowdstrike EDR endpoint detection to find the detection details using the host name.

 

  1.  As we have different types of IOAs first we need to understand the custom IOA rule configured for this detection.
  2. If the detected IOA is related to the domain, we will go into host selection or module in falcon in the networking tab. We can get to see all the domain activity associated with the host.
  3. We will export the csv file to carry out the further analysis to verify if the IOA rule listed domain exists or not.
  4. We will try to check DNS events just before the detection to verify if it is redirected from any other url.
  5. To double check the redirection we will run the URL in the KASM secured environment then inspect on the page to check the networking activity of the URL.
  6. Then we will check the base filename which created the DNS activity in the event search of the falcon.
  7. As part of remediation activity we will create the request for browser reset if URL connected by the browser like chrome or edge
  8. After checking, if no downloads are observed in the command line we will write the user about device usage policy and also we will create a networking ticket to block the URL into the proxy.

topics.title: what is cyber security?
topics.content: Cyber Security or computer security, is the practice of protecting computer systems, networks, and data from theft, damage, or unauthorized access. It involves implementing measures to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information in digital form. With the increasing reliance on technology and the internet, Cyber Security has become a critical aspect of safeguarding individuals, organizations, and governments from cyber threats.

topics.title: HUB
topics.content: Hub is a layer 1 device that connects two or more computers, it will broadcast the data to allthe devices connected on the network.

topics.title: SWITCH
topics.content: Switch is a layer 2 device which connects two or more computers, here the data will be sentto the dedicated devices by doing unicast.

topics.title: ROUTER
topics.content: It is a layer 3 device which connects two or more networks, it will finds the best route tosend the data from one network to another network.

topics.title: IP ADDRESSES
topics.content:
IP address is the series of numbers that identifies each device over the internet. It is also called as logical addressing. There are 2 types of IP addresses

  1. Private IP Range
    1. 10.0.0.0 – 10.255.255.255
    2. 172.16.0.0 - 172.31.255.255
    3. 192.168.0.0 – 192.168.255.255
  2. Public IP Range
    1. 1.0.0.0 – 126.255.255.255
    2. 128.0.0.0 – 191.255.255.255
    3. 192.0.0.0 – 223.255.255.255
    4. 224.0.0.0 – 239.255.255.255 = for multi casting
    5. 240.0.0.0 – 255.255.255.255 = reserved for experiment/ research

topics.title: NAT
topics.content: NAT stands for NETWORK ADDRESS TRANSLATION. It converts the private IP to public IP andvice-versa.

topics.title: PAT
topics.content: PAT stands for PORT ADDRESS TRANSLATION. It maps multiple devices on a LAN to single public IP address.

topics.title: PORT NUMBER
topics.content:
It is the communication end points. It is the logical address of each application. Port number is 16 bits. There are total 0- 65,535 port numbers available. 

  • 0 – 1023 = well known port numbers for prominent companies.
  • 1024 – 49151 = Those who want to register specific ports, can chose from this.
  • 49152 – 65535 = Dynamic ports, available for anyone to choose.

topics.title: DIFF BETWEEN TCP AND UDP
3-WAY HANDSHAKE METHOD
topics.content:
A 3-way handshake is a method in a TCP/IP network to create a connection between two hosts. 

It is a 3-step process that requires both the client and server to exchange SYNand ACK before actual data communication begins. 

  • A client node sends a SYN data packet to a server it wants to communicate to.The objective of this packet is to ask if the server is ready to open for new connections.
  • If the server is willing to communicate to the client (if the port is open) it responds with an ACK packet. It also expresses its intention of talking back to the client with itsSYN packet. Together it is SYN/ACK 

  • The client node responds with an ACK for the servers SYN. 

    Upon completion of this process, the connection is created and the host and server cancommunicate.

topics.title: TCP/IP Packet structure
topics.content:
A packet has 3 main sections 

  • IP header
  • TCP header 

  • Payload 

    In this few of the important fields in the packets are Source IP, Destination IP, Source Port, Destination Port, TCP Flags, Data.

topics.title: FLAGS USED IN TCP CONNECTION
topics.content:
Flags :- Flags helps to identify the status of the communication. 

  1. SYN: it is used in first step of connection establishment phase or 3-way handshakeprocess b/w the two hosts.
  2. ACK: it is used to acknowledge packet which are successful received by the host.
  3. FIN: it is used to request for connection termination.
  4. RST: it is used to terminate the connection if the RST sender feels something is wrongwith the TCP connection or that the conversation should not exist.
  5. PUSH: It is used to indicate that the receiving device should deliver the data tothe receiving application as soon as possible, rather than buffering it.
  6. URG: It is used to notify the receiver to process the urgent packets beforeprocessing all other packets.

topics.title: OSI MODEL (OPEN SYSTEM INTERCONNECTION)
topics.content:
It is reference model, for understanding how the data is communicated b/w two hosts. It contains 7 layer each layer specified functions, this approach from bottom to top.

 

  1. APPLICATION LAYER: interface b/w user and computer, it provides services tothe user, applications produce the data, which has to be transferred over the network. (Protocols: Http, SMTP) (Data).
  2. PRESENTATION LAYER: the data from the application layer is extracted here and manipulated as per the required format to transmit over the network. (JPEG, MPEG, TLS, SSL). Its major functions are
    1. Translation
    2. Compression
    3. Encryption
  3. SESSION LAYER: this layer is responsible for establishment of connection, maintenance of session, authentication and also ensure security. (NETBIOS, RPC). Its major functions are
    1. Authentication- Verifying who is the user
    2. Authorization- Server gives the permission to authenticated user to access the resources.
  4. TRANSPORT LAYER: It is the heart of the OSI model. It provides reliable message delivery from process to process, ensures that messages are transmitted in the order in which they are sent and there is no duplication of data. Port number and sequence number addressing is done in this layer. Data is transmitted in the form of packets. (TCP/UDP). Its major functions are
    1. Flow control
    2. Error control
  5. NETWORK LAYER: Network layer works for the transmission of data from one host to the other located in different networks. Logical addressing (IP addressing) is done in this layer. Data is transmitted in the form of Frames. (RIP, OSPF). Its major functions are
    1. Logical addressing
    2. Routing
    3. Path Determination
  6. DATA LINK LAYER: the data link layer is responsible for the node-tonode delivery of the message, it does framing, error control, flow control etc. Here the physical addressing (MAC addressing) is done. (ARP).

  7. PHYSICAL LAYER: It is responsible for the actual physical connection b/w thedevices. (Hub,WiFi) (Bits).

    Physical layer, Datalink layer, Network layer are the Hardware layers. Transport layer is the heart of the OSI. Session, Presentation and Applicationlayers are the Software layers.

topics.title: CYBER ATTACKS ON OSI LAYER:
topics.content:
• Application: SQL injection, cross site scripting
  • Presentation: encryption, decryption attack.
  • Session: MITM, secure shell, sniffing.
  • Transportation: SYN flood attack, UDP flood attack, DOS attack.
  • Network: IP Spoofing, Packet Sniffing.
  • Data link: ARP spoofing, DHCP attack.
  • Physical: Data sniffing, physical damage, unauthorized access

topics.title: DNS (DOMAIN NAME SYSTEM)
topics.content:
It is a service that helps in translating domain names to IP addresses and vice versa.

  • When a computer needs to reach to a domain (like facebook.com) it sends a request to a server called DNS Resolver (DNS server). if the mapping is found for the domain in the DNS cache, the server returns the IP address. 

  • If not The resolver reaches out to root server. Root server holds the index of atop-level domains. There are 13 root servers globally. 

  • TLD Name server gives the IP address of the authoritative name server that holds the mapping for the requested domain name.

  • If the authoritative name server has access to the requested record, it will return the IP address. This address is return to the client that madethe original request.

  • The client now makes the request to the IP address and get the response

topics.title: DHCP (DYNAMIC HOST CONFIGURATION PROTOCOL)
topics.content:
DHCP server automatically assigns an IP address and other information to eachhost on the network so they can communicate with other endpoints.

DHCP works on a process called DORA.

  • When a computer that is configured to get the IP details automatically ispowered on, it sends DHCP Discover message to all hosts.

  • After the DHCP server receives Discover message it suggests the IPaddressing offering to the client host by unicast.

  • This OFFER message contains IP address, subnet mask, default gateway,DNS and lease period.

  • Now after the client receives the offer it requests the informationofficially sending REQUEST message to server this time by unicast.

  • Server sends ACKNOWLEDGE message confirming the DHCP lease toclient. Now client is allowed to use new IP settings.

topics.title: ARP (ADDRESS RESOULTION PROTOCOL)
topics.content:
It helps to resolve an IP address to physical address (MAC ADDRESS)Works

  • When a source device wants to communicate with another device, source device checks its ARP Cache to find it already has a resolved MACaddress of the destination device. If it is there, it will use that MAC address for communication. If not, the source broadcasts the ARP request message to the local network.

  • The message is received by each device on the LAN since it is a broadcast. When the destination device receives the ARP request, it willsend the ARP reply message to the source as a unicast.

  • The sources machine will update its ARP cache.

topics.title: PROXY
topics.content:
Proxy server works on behalf of the requested computer basically proxy server helps to hides the identity of the user from internet to intranet.

Apart from hiding the identity, proxy provides the multiple benefits, whichincludes,

  1. Monitoring the internet activity.
  2. Monitoring bandwidth consumption.
  3. Blacklist and Whitelist the domains.
  4. Categorize the domains.
  5. we can implement access control.

Note: But Proxy just changes the IP address but it can’t encrypt the data. (so for encrypt the data we need to use VPN)

topics.title: PORT NUMBERS
FIREWALL
topics.content:
Firewall is a network security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on the predetermined security rules. These rules can configure in ACL (Access control list). Rules can be based on IP address, port numbers, protocols, Domain names, Key words.

 

ACTIONS OF FIREWALL:

ALLOWED, BLOCKED, DROP, DENY.

 

 

TYPES OF FIREWALL

  1. Packet filtering FW: Which filters the data packets passing through it.
  2. Stateless (Dynamic packet filtering) FW: Apart from packet filtering, it also keeps track of it.
  3. Next gen FW: Along with traditional FW, it has the advanced features of IPS and IDS.
  4. Proxy FW: Acts as the intermediary between user and the internet.

topics.title: IPS
topics.content:
• IPS stand for Intrusion Prevention System
  • IPS works on the principle like compares the current network traffic and known threat database and take the action.
  • If it observes any malicious traffic then it will block the traffic immediately.
  • And IPS acts as a Control system.
  • IPS work on the basis of signature.

topics.title: IDS
topics.content:
• IDS stand for Intrusion Detection System
  • IDS works on the principle like compares the current network traffic and known threat database and take the action.
  • If it observes any malicious traffic then it creates an alert to admin to take the action.
  • And IDS acts as a Monitoring system.
  • IPS work on the basis of Network Behavior.

topics.title: MZ (De-militarized Zone)
topics.content: DMZ is the additional layer of network security, which segregates the system and servers on the opposite line of FW. The DMZ isolates the public facing servers from internal servers.

topics.title: WAF (Web Application Firewall)
topics.content:
WAF is the network security device, that secures the network at the application layer (L7) level by filtering and monitoring HTTP and HTTPS traffic between the web application and internet.

WAF protects the organization from different type of application layer attacks such as,

  • Cross site scripting (XSS)
  • SQL Injection
  • DoS, DDoS
  • Zero day attack etc.

topics.title: VPN (Virtual Private Network)
topics.content:
It is a secured tunnel b/w your device and the internet.

VPN changes users IP address and encrypt the data, transfer b/w the device and internet, allowing the private IP and secure web browsing.

topics.title: DIFFERENCE BETWEEN SSL AND TLS:
topics.content:
SSL:

  • When a computer connects to a website, which is using SSL, the web browser will ask the website to identify itself.
  • Web server will send the copy of its SSL certificate to web browser.
  • SSL certificate is the small digital certificate, that is used to authenticate the identity of the website.
  • Basically it is used to let your computer know that website you are using is trustworthy.
  • So browser will check the certificate and send a message to the web browser, in return web server will sends the acknowledgement.
  • Now encrypted data can be shared between web browser and web server.

TLS:

  • It is the latest industry standard cryptographic protocol. (It is advance method of SSL)

It works based on the same specifications like SSL.

  • But, Here both web server and web browser is authenticated

topics.title: CIA TRAID
topics.content:
Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability, also known as CIA Triad. It is a model designed to guide policies for information security with an organization.

 

CONFIDENTIALITY

Confidentiality means that only authorized peoples can access the sensitive information of an organization. This can be achieved with the help of encryption and implementation of access control.

INTEGRITY

Ensuring the data is not modified either in transit or at storage. Even if it is modified only authorized persons can do it. This can be achieved with the help of Hashing.

AVAILABILITY

Ensuring the systems and data readily available to it’s users. This can be achieved with the help of Redundancy, Backups and Load balancers.

topics.title: ENCRYPTION
topics.content:
It is a process of encoding the information in such a way that only authorized parties can only understanding it. the encryption it is done by sharing keys. And Encryption is used to ensure the confidentiality of the data. And it is two way process i.e. we can get the data back by decryption.

TYPES OF ENCRYPTION

1) Symmetric: Same key is used for encryption and decryption. (Shared key for both)

2) Asymmetric: Different Key is used for encryption and decryption. (Public key for encryption and Private key for decryption)

topics.title: HASHING
topics.content:
It is a process of transformation of a string of characters into a fixed length of value or key. That represents the original string. Hashing is a one-way process i.e. we cannot get the data back from hash value. Hashing is used to ensure the integrity of the data.

 

Example: MD5, SHA1, SHA256

topics.title: VULNERABILIRTY
topics.content:
It is a weakness or gaps in a security program that can be exploited by threats to gain the unauthorized access to an asset.

Example: Unpatched software and weak passwords.

topics.title: THREAT
topics.content: Anything that can be exploit a vulnerability, intentionally or accidentally to obtain damage or destroy an asset.

topics.title: RISK
topics.content: A potential for loss or damage which can occur when the vulnerability gets exploited.

topics.title: EXPLOIT
topics.content: It is a tool or a technique that takes the advantage of vulnerability to carry out the cyber-attack.

topics.title: ZERO TRUST MODEL
topics.content:
It is an IT security model that requires strict identity verification for every person and devicetrying to access resources on private network, regardless they are sitting within or outside of the network perimeter.

Few principles of zero trust model are:

  • Assume there are attackers both inside and outside the network.
  • Concept of least privilege access.
  • Use multi factor authentication whenever possible.

topics.title: TYPES OF TRAFFICS
topics.content:
INBOUND TRAFFIC: The traffic generates outside of the organization and it is connected tointernal system is called inbound traffic.

OUTBOUND TRAFFIC : the traffic initiates from the internal IP and trying to reach outthrough external IP in the internet.

topics.title: ESS
topics.content: It is defined as dedicated security solution adapted by organization monitor the incoming and outgoing mails for various threats such as spam phishing and malware it worksby identifying the sender email address scanning the content of grammatical mistakes, samesubject line, urgency in mail, url in the body and scanning the attachment associated in the mail.

topics.title: DEFENSE IN DEPTH (DID)
topics.content:
It is the layered security approach, which helps to secure the tangible and in tangible assets of an organization.

This method allows defense team to identify the cyber-attack, as this approach extends time taken for attack.

topics.title: SYSTEM HARDENING:
topics.content:
System hardening is the process of securing a system by reducing the attack surface.

Few things on the system hardening checklist includes:

  • Changing the default user credentials.
  • Closing all unused ports.
  • Stopping all unused services.
  • Install updates and patches.
  • Implement Access Control.
  • Install Antivirus and keep the signatures up to date.

topics.title: TYPES OF HACKERS
topics.content:
1. White hat hackers: They are authorized hackers, who work for the govt. and organizations by performing penetration testing and identifying loopholes in their cyber security.
  2. Black hat hackers: These are hackers, who hack for malicious intentions, like financial gain.
  3. Grey hat hackers: They are not legally authorized hackers they work with good and bad intentions; they can use their skills for personal gain.

topics.title: WIRESHARKS
topics.content: Wireshark is the free and open source packet analyzer. It is used for network troubleshooting, analysis, software and communication protocol development and education.

topics.title: CYBER KILL CHAIN
topics.content:
It is a step-by-step process carried out by an attacker, when attacker sets a target which needs to be compromised.

As a defender it is essential to understand the cyber kill chain so we can detect and defend the cyber attacks at every possible phases.

There are 7 phases in cyber kill chain

  1. RECONNAISSANCE: In this stage the attacker gathers information about the target such as identifying potential vulnerabilities, network architecture and employees. This can involves scanning public information, social engineering or other methods to gain intelligence.
  2. WEAPONIZATION: Once the attacker gathers enough information then the attacker develop and create a malicious payload, such as a virus, Trojan, or exploit.
  3. DELIVERY: The attacker delivers the weaponized payload to the target, often through methods like phishing mail or malicious websites.
    • That can be defended by with the help of email security solution and proxy by whitelisting.
  4. EXPLOITATION: Once the delivery is successful the weapons code is triggered and exploiting vulnerable applications or system.
    • That can be defended with the help of proper vulnerability assessment.
  5. INSTALLATION: In this point the attacker tries to create the backdoor to gain the access on the targeted system.
    • With the help of EDR we can detect the installation bymonitor the outbound traffic.
  6. COMMAND AND CONTROL: The attacker establishes a connection to the compromised system to control it remotely.
    • With the help of monitoring the networktraffic to unknown domain and IP address.
  7. ACTION ON OBJECTIVE: The attacker works to achieve their objective. Which includes data theft, ex-exfiltration or destruption of data or intrusion of another target.

topics.title: MITER ATTACK
topics.content:
It is a Comprehensive framework which helps to identify the TTP’s used by the attacker to carry out the cyber attack.

This framework contains 14 tactics and 250+ techniques.

With the help of this framework we can create use-cases and alerts with-in the organizational risk.

Tactics are the attacker technical goals. Techniques are how those goals are achieved. Procedure specific implementation of techniques

There are 14 tactics

  1. Reconnaissance: The advisory trying to gather information they can used plan future operations.
  2. Resource development: The advisory trying to establish resources they can use to support operations.
  3. Initial access: The advisory trying to get into your network.
  4. Execution: the advisory trying to run malicious code.
  5. Persistence: the advisory trying to maintain their foothold.
  6. Privilege escalation: the advisory trying to gain higher level permissions.
  7. Defense evasion: the advisory trying to avoid being detected
  8. Credential access: the advisory trying to steal account names and password
  9. Discovery: the advisory trying to figure out your environment.
  10. 10.Lateral movement: the advisory trying to move through your environment.
  11. 11.Collection: the advisory trying to gather data of interest to their goal
  12. 12.Command and control: the advisory trying to communicate with compromised systems to control them.
  13. 13.Exfiltration: the advisory trying to steal data.
  14. 14.Impact: the advisory trying to manipulate, interrupt or destroy your systems and data.

topics.title: HTTP RESPONSE CODES:
topics.content:
• These are 3 digit numeric codes, that are returned by web server in response to a client’s request made to website.
  • They provide information about the outcome of the request and indicate whether it was successful or encountered an error. These codes are-
  1. 1XX= Informational: It means the request has been received and the process is continuing.
  2. 2XX= Success: It means action was successfully received, understood and accepted.
  3. 3XX= Redirection: It means further action must be taken in order to complete the request.
  4. 4XX= Client error: It means the request contains in correct syntax or cannot be fulfilled.
  5. 5XX= Server Error: It means server failed to fulfil an apparently valid request.

topics.title: BRUTE FORCE ATTACK: (Password guessing attack)
topics.content:
It’s a type of cyber attack where the attacker uses the different combination of user name and password to gain unauthorized access.

Mitigation:

  • use the complex password
  • use Multi Factor Authentication
  • Use captcha to slow-Down brute force
  • Implement rate limit (No.of Logins per day)
  • Password Reset policy

topics.title: DICTIONARY ATTACK
topics.content:
It’s a type of brute-force attack where attacker uses the list of words in dictionary as password to gain unauthorized access.

Also uses target personal details like DOB, Children name, Vechicle no as password.

topics.title: RAINBOW ATTACK
topics.content:
It’s a type of brute-force attack where attacker uses pre-computed hash values as password, instead of trying to pass the password, attacker tries to match the hash in the user database.

Mitigation:

  • Use Salt technique
  • Use MFA
  • Use captcha

topics.title: SCANNING
topics.content:
Scanning is method for discovering exploitable communication channels. Scanning for open ports.

Scanning for known vulnerabilities.

Mitigation:

  • Use Firewall and IPS.
  • OS Hardening.
  • Use honeypots to detect scanning activities.

 

TYPES OF SCANNING:

Horizontal scan: Is a type of scan that sends the request to same port on different host.

Vertical scan: Here the attacker sends the request to discover multiple ports on a single host.

topics.title: TYPES OF ATTACKS:
topics.content:
1. Flood attack
  2. Password attack
  3. Scanning
  4. Sniffing
  5. Spoofing
  6. DNS attack
  7. Phishing

topics.title: SPOOFING
topics.content:
It is a type of cyber attack, this technique used by the attacker to impersonate original attributes, which includes the malicious intent.

Example: (Fake email id, fake web sites, URLs) which exactly seems like an original one so that user can be trapped or scammed

Few types of spoofing:

  • IP spoofing
  • Mac address spoofing
  • Email spoofing
  • DNS spoofing

Mitigation:

  • Deploy IPS (IP spoofing).
  • Educate users (email spoofing).
  • Enable port level security (ARP and MAC address spoofing).

topics.title: SNIFFING ATTACK
topics.content:
A sniffing attack occurs when an attacker uses a packet sniffer to intercept and read the sensitive data passing through a network.

Mitigation:

  • Avoid using insecure protocols (Like HTTP, FTP Telnet etc. and use secured versions like HTTPS, SFTP, SSH etc.)
  • Use encryption whenever possible for data transmission.

topics.title: PHISHING ATTACK:
topics.content:
It’s a type of cyber attack where attacker uses the email as a weapon to target to the individuals by attaching the malicious link/URL in the attachment in the phished mail.

Here the goal of the attacker is to make the user to click on the URL or download the attachment.

Mitigations:

  • Use email security solutions (to block obvious phishing and spam emails)
  • Educate users
  • Use DMARC [Domain based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance].

 

Other phishing attack: Spear phishing:

It’s a type of phishing attack where attacker sends the modified and personalized phishing mails to the selected individual instead of sending in mass.

Whaling:

It’s a type of phishing attack where attacker targets top management of organization by using the phishing mails.

Whishing:

It works as same as phishing instead of sending email the attacker tricks the target to give critical/sensitive information over phone call.

topics.title: EMAIL AUTHENTICATORS
topics.content:
1. SPF: Sender Policy Framework, which helps to authenticate weather the email came from the authenticated user or not, by comparing the the sender domain names to its IP address.
  2. DKIM: Domain Key Identified Mail, This helps to validate the integrity of the mail to make sure the mail is not tamper, when it is flowing through the different servers by comparing or validating the cryptographic signature.

DMARC: (Domain based Message Authentication Reporting and Conformance)

It is a combination of both SPF and DKIM, which validates both authentication and authorization.

topics.title: SALTING
topics.content: It is the process of improving the security of the hash value by adding the alpha- numeric values before and after the actual hash value.

topics.title: TRACEROUTE
topics.content:
It is the network diagnostic tool, used to trace the route that data packets take from one computer to another over the network.

It uses the ICMP, TCP, UDP protocols.

Command= “tracert _ host name/IP”

topics.title: ZERODAY
topics.content: It refers to the software vulnerability, that is exploited by attackers on the same day it is discovered.

topics.title: DWELL TIME
topics.content: Dwell time refers to the amount of time that a cyber threat or attacker remains undetected within a network after gaining unauthorized access.

topics.title: BOT SCORE
topics.content:
• It is the score from 1 to 99, that indicates how likely that request came from a bot.

 

  • Bot scores are available to be used in Firewall fields.

topics.title: DOS and DDOS ATTACKS
topics.content:
DOS: Denial of service is a type of cyber attack from one attacker against to single target. It Denial of service is intended to make a system resources or services unavailable to legitimate users.

DDOS: DDOS attack is a type of attack, where the multiple systems are used to launch DOS attack on one target. Most of the attacker use the Botnet malware to execute DDOS attack.

topics.title: TCP SYN FLOOD ATTACK
topics.content:
It is a type of DOS attack, where is exploits the normal TCP Three-way Handshake. The attacker sends the huge connection requests (SYN) but never sends an acknowledge back to the server. This will make the server wait for certain time and hold the connection. This will consumes all the concurrent connections on the target server making it inaccessible for legit users.

MITIGATIONS:

  • Use Anti-DDOS technology (like Arbor).
  • Rate limit(limit the numbers of connection from an IP or user)
  • Reduce the connection wait time.
  • Deploy load balancers.
  • Block the particular IP address.

topics.title: ARP POISING
topics.content:
It is type of cyber attack attacker sends falsified MAC address to LAN and update in the ARP table so the attacker can redirect the packets to the attacker system.

Mitigation: - Use Static ARP

-Detect ARP poisoning using tools like XARP

-Setup Packet Filtering

-Install AV and keep signatures updated

topics.title: MAN IN THE MIDDLE ATTACK (MITM)
topics.content:
It is the type of cyber attack where attacker secretly relays and possibly alters the communication between 2 users, who believe that they are directly communicating with each other.

Mitigation: - Use Static ARP

-Use encryption

-IPS system (can detect sudden change in the network performance)

topics.title: DNS POISIONING
topics.content:
It is a type of cyber attack that exploits vulnerability in the domain name system (DNS) to divert internet traffic away from legitimate servers and towards fake once.

Mitigation:

  • Regularly audit DNS zones.
  • Keeping DNS servers up-to-date.
  • Restrict zone transfers.
  • Limit resources queries.
  • Store only data related to the requested domain.

topics.title: DNS TUNNELING
topics.content:
Attacker includes the malicious data or sensitive data in the packet and sends request through port no 53 so the firewall will allow the traffic on port no 53 so that attacker can bypass the firewall and enter into internal network. Exfilterate or injects the system.

Mitigation:

  • IPS system can help detect few DNS Tunneling attack.
  • Block the communication to IP’s that are known to be use for data exfiltration.
  • Use a DNS firewall
  • Deploy standalone DNS protection solution ( like Infoblox).

topics.title: MALWARE
topics.content:
Malware or malicious software is any program or file that intentionally harmful to a computer or computer network.

TYPES OF MALWARE:

VIRUS: It attach themselves clean files and infects other clean files.

TROJAN: It is a type of malware it seem to be legitimate file but contents malicious intent.

WORM: It is a type of malware it infect the entire network without user interaction.

BOTNET: These are the networks which are infects the computer that are made to work together under the control of an attacker

SPYWARE: It is a malware designed to spy on you.it hides in the background and takes notes on what you do online including your passwords credit card no’s surfing habits and more.

Ransomware: These kind of malware typically locks down the computers, files and threatens to erase everything unless you pay a Ransom.

ADWARE: Through tough not always malicious in nature aggressive advertising software can undermine your security just to serve the AD’s, which can give other malware an easy way in and also they wind up the consuming system resources.

RAT: [Remote access Trojan]: It is a type of malware that allows an attacker gain unauthorized remote access of victims machine.

topics.title: OWASP (OPEN WEB APPLICATION SECURITY PROJECT)
topics.content:
It is an online community which helps to identify the top 10 vulnerabilities. So that developers can develop secure web application by testing these vulnerabilities.

Every year OWASP announces list of Top 10 Vulnerabilities for Web Applications- OWASP Top 10 As 2023, top web applications Vulnerabilities are

TOP 10 OWASP are:

  1. Broken Access Control 

  2. Cryptographic failure

  3. Injection

  4. Insecure design

  5. Security Misconfiguration

  6. Vulnerable and Outdated Components

  7. Identification and Authentication Failures

  8. Software and Data Integrity Failures

  9. Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

  10. Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

topics.title: SQL INJECTION:
topics.content:
It is a type of server side cyber attack.

SQL injection is a code injection technique, in which malicious SQL statements inserted into an entry field for execution.

By executing malicious statements, attacker can gain unauthorized access, copy, modify, delete the data.

For eg:

If a web application uses a logging from that accepts user name and password an attacker could enter malicious SQL code in user name field that tricks the application into giving the attacker access to the entire data base.

Mitigations:-

  • Input validation.
  • Sanitize all inputs (like remove quotes and special characters).
  • Use IPS and WAF solution.
  • Turn off visibility of database errors on production servers.

topics.title: CROSS SITE SCRIPTING (XSS)
topics.content:
It is a type of client-side cyber attack, where the attacker will introduces the malicious script into the entry field of the website where the users accessed. By introduction the malicious script and exploiting of the vulnerability the attacker captures the user information includes Credential information, Card details, Browsing history.

Mitigation:

  • Input validation.
  • Sanitize all inputs (like remove quotes and special characters).
  • Encode data on output.

topics.title: CSRF (CROSS SITE REQUEST FORGERY)
topics.content:
CSRF attack exploits the trust that web application has in an authenticated user.

CSRF is web application vulnerability in which server does not check whether the request came from a trusted client or not. the request is just processed directly .it can be further followed by the ways to detect this examples, and count measures.

topics.title: VULNERABILTY ASSEMENT
topics.content:
It is a red team activity which involves in identifying the vulnerabilities organization system and application.

The process starts with creation of the batches and scheduling the scanned reports distributed among different departments with vulnerability and recommendations to update or fix the vulnerability.

topics.title: DATA EXFILTERATION
topics.content: Leakage of data without being detected to authorized person

topics.title: LATERAL MOVEMENT
topics.content: It is like moving file in the LAN from compromised system through FTP.

topics.title: NTLM and KERBEROS
topics.content:
Both NTLM and Kerberos are windows authentication mechanism,

  • Where in NTLM uses the challenge mechanism for authentication which means credentials are validated by converting into hashes.

 

  • The Kerberos uses the Third party symmetric encryption called KDC (Key Distribution Center) through which by providing the TGT (Ticket granting Ticket) and TGS (Ticket Granting Service) the secure authentication will be performance.

 

Apart from that NTLM doesn’t provide the SSO (Single Sign-On) and NTLM is vulnerable compare to Kerberos.

topics.title: AAA
topics.content:
Authentication: Used to verify the identity of a person.

Authorization: The process of verifying that somebody has the appropriate permission to access something.

Accounting: The process of recording a user's access by means of logging their activity.

topics.title: SECURITY MISCONFIGURATION
topics.content: it is a vulnerability when a device and application and network is configured in a way that can be exploited by an attacker to take advantage of it this can be as simple as leaving the default user name password unchanged or too simple for device accounts etc.

topics.title: SIEM (Security information and event management)
topics.content:
SIEM stands for Security information and event management, which is a security monitoring tool, which helps to detect and analyze the security events happening throughout the organization network by detecting with the help of setting the correlation rules, where all the log sources are integrated to SIEM for effective monitoring of network traffic.

The SIEM performs the log activities includes Normalization, Aggregation and Parsing.

topics.title: SPLUNK ES ARCHITECTURE
topics.content:
Splunk ES is a SIEM solution which contains 3 main components, which are

  1. Forwarder
  2. Indexer
  3. Search head
  4. Forwarder:- It is an agent which will be installed on the log sources from where we need to fetch the logs.

There are 2 types of forwarders

  • Universal forwarder: it will forwards the raw data without doing any prior treatments like indexing and normalizing.
  • Heavy forwarder: it will perform some parsing and indexing activity beforesending the logs to the indexer.
  1. Indexer :- Indexer acts as a directory where it will store the data based on source type and time of log.

There are 4 types of indexers, which are generally called as buckets, Where the logs will be stored based on the freshness of the log from Hot bucket to worm bucket to cold bucket to Frozen bucket. Where the frozen bucket logs can’t be accessed from the search head.

 

  1. Search head: - which provides user interface to the user to access and fetch the logs from different log sources for the purpose of analysis by using SPL (Splunk processing language).

ACTIVITIES PERFORMED ON THE SPLUNK:

  1. Analysis of alerts
  2. Fine tuning of alerts
  3. Creation of the use case
  4. Creation of the reports
  5. Creation of the dashboards
  6. Creation of the Macros

DEFAULT PORTS IN THE SPLUNK:

  1. 514- Splunk network port
  2. 8000- Splunk web port
  3. 8080- Splunk Index replication port
  4. 8089- Management port
  5. 8191- KV store
  6. 9997- Splunk indexing port

topics.title: QRADAR ARCHITECTURE
topics.content:
In QRadar architecture has mainly 3 components

  1. Data collection
  2. Data processor
  3. Data search
    1. Data collection: - The data is passed and normalized before it passes to the data processing layer.

Event data: Represents events that occurs at a point in a time in the user environment such as user login, email, VPN connection, firewalldenies, firewall allows, proxy connection.

Flow data:- It is a network activity information or session information b/w the two hosts on a network, which Qradar transmits into flow records.

  1. Data processing:- In data processing layer where event data and flow data are run through custom rule engine (CRE) which given offenses and alertsand then the data is return to storage.
  2. Data search:- In the 3rd layer data that is collected and processed

by Qradar isunstable to users for searching analysis, reporting and alerts or offense for investigation.

topics.title: PARSING
topics.content:
• Parsing is process of converting unstructured data into structured format.
  • It is during parsing where SIEM extracts all the useful metadata like source IP,destination IP, user name, file name, file hash etc. from the logs.

topics.title: NORMALIZATION
topics.content:
• Normalization is a process of bringing all events into one common structure to deliver a homogeneous view.
  • It could be time normalization (bring events from various devices from different Geo-location to a common time-zone).
  • Identifying common event attributes (like categorization – stamping all login, logout events as authentication).

Note: FOR some SIEM tools Normalization=Parsing.

topics.title: AGGREGATION
topics.content:
• It is the process of merging similar logs that occur over a period of time.
  • For Example, If there are 20 failed login events by a user on a server, the server would generate 20 logs, but instead of storing all the 20 logs, SIEM will only store 1 record.
  • Aggregation greatly helps is conserving the disk space and also increases the performance.

topics.title: CO-RELATION
topics.content:
Co-relation can be defined as set of condition that indicates a suspicious activity.

Example:

  • User activity during non-business hours
  • VPN logins from multiple locations
  • Multiple malwares on the same host.

topics.title: WINDOWS EVENT LOGS
topics.content:
1. 4624 – Successful user account login
  2. 4625 – failed user account login
  3. 4720 – a user account is created
  4. 4726 – a user account was deleted
  5. 4740 – a user account was locked out
  6. 4767 – a user account was unlocked
  7. 1102 – the audit log was cleared

There are 3 main categories in windows event logs

  1. Application: these logs record the events related to application running on the windows operating system.

EX: if an application crashes the details of the crash will be recorded in the application logs.

  1. Security: the event related to security logs on the window operating system recorded as security logs.

EX: user login activity

  1. System: this logs records the event related to window OS itself EX: if any drives fail to load or hardware device malware function

topics.title: IOC (INDICATOR OF COMPROMISE)
topics.content:
IOC Stands for indicators of compromise, it’s an attribute associated with an attack

IOC focuses on what of an attack, Attributes associated with an attack might include – IP address, URL, Email, File hash etc.

topics.title: IOA (INDICATOR OF ATTACK)
topics.content: IOAs are derived from known attack techniques, tactics, and procedures (TTPs) employed by threat actors. They are often created based on threat intelligence and security research to help security analysts identify suspicious activities that may indicate an ongoing attack.

topics.title: PICERL (INCIDENT REVIEW PROCESS)
topics.content:
Preparation: This step involves creating an incident response plan,outlining roles and responsibilities, and training personnel. For example, a company might create a plan that outlines how to respond to a data breach, assign specific roles to employees, and train them on how to respond to the breach.

Identification: In this step, the incident is identified and verified. Thismay involve monitoring systems, reviewing logs, and analyzing network traffic. For example, an organization might detect an unauthorized user accessing their system through suspicious activity alerts or anomalies.

Containment: Once an incident has been identified, the next step isto contain it to prevent further damage. This might involve isolating affected systems, blocking access to networks, or shutting down servers. For example, an organization might disconnect an infected machine from the network to stop the spread of malware.

Eradication: This step involves removing the threat from affected systems. This might involve cleaning infected machines, patching vulnerabilities, or rebuilding systems. For example, an organization might remove malware from a machine using antivirus software.

Recovery: After the threat has been removed, the next step is to restore systems and data to their previous state. This might involve restoring data from backups or rebuilding systems from scratch. For example, an organization might restore a database from a backup after it was encrypted by ransomware.

Lessons Learned: Finally, the incident response team should conduct a post- incident review to identify areas for improvement and update the incident response plan accordingly. This might involve analyzing the incident to determine its root cause, evaluating the effectiveness of the response, and documenting lessons learned. For example, an organization might realize they need to improve their access control measures to prevent future incidents.

 

 

Overall, the PICERL process provides a structured approach to incident response, enabling organizations to quickly and effectivelyrespond to cyber security incidents.

topics.title: FINETUNING OF ALERTS
topics.content:
• It’s a process carried out to identify the expected pattern of the alerts to create the exceptions, so that FP alerts will be reduced.
  • If we observe flood of repeated alerts and once we go through the analysis, and after getting confirmation from the respective owner about the activity, we tried to create the exceptions by identifying the specific user, IP, Host name, threshold or by tuning the misconfiguration with the alert.
  • Generally, we follow the fine tuning process, starting from identifying the exceptions, validating the exceptions, and creating the change request (CR) presenting the CR to the client.
  • Once we get the approval, we create the ticket to the Splunk operation team to update co-relation search and once we get the confirmation, we maintain the SIEM log change database.
  • Some of the fine tuning carried out on-
    1. Excessive SMB connection: In this alert, we identified and excluded the domain controllers (DC) and some of the Azure IP, because after migration, some of the IPs have changed to Azure IP.
    2. Geographically Improbable access detected: Here we excluded some of the VPN segment IPs of our organization.
    3. Active directory excessive login per host: Here we identified and excluded the file print servers.
    4. User reported phishing mail: Here we increased threshold from reported by one user to three users.

topics.title: USE CASE CREATION
topics.content:
• As we working for the client, we have limited exposure to create the use case but during the May 2022, there was a Microsoft vulnerability reported which is MSDT. During that time, I was part of creating the use case working with the client.
  • There we first identified the log source needed to create the alert, which is event log in this case.
  • Then we identified the path of the process where the RCE (Remote Code Execution) happening, which is-

Relative _Target_Name=”Windows\\system32\\msdt.exe”

and we set the priority level to critical

After configuring the alert, we started receiving flood of alerts and when we go through the analysis, our SVC scan used to create lot of benign alerts, so later we excluded the SVC scan from co-relation search.

topics.title: DOMAIN CONTROLLER (DC)
topics.content:
It is the server, that provides authentication and authorization services for an AD domain.
